hero_intro: Welcome to the Brubru EFPIA Brief. Every weekday until 28 June you receive a short read of what moved in EU pharma and health policy in the last 24 hours. You also see what Brubru is tracking for you, and what the agent itself has learned today. Five items below.

headlines.title: The Commission published the full analysis behind the Biotech Act
headlines.snippet: The Commission has now published the evidence document that sits underneath the Biotech Act, both the Regulation and the companion Directive on genetically modified microorganisms. The seven pillars are confirmed, the budget envelope of 20.4 billion euros under the next financial framework is confirmed, and the three new governance bodies are spelled out. The proposal is still on the table at the European Parliament. No rapporteur has been appointed for procedure 2025/0406(COD) and no committee vote is scheduled.
headlines.ask: What does the Biotech Act analysis cover and what is its status in the European Parliament?

headlines.title: The next EMA CHMP meeting is 22 to 25 June in Amsterdam
headlines.snippet: The next CHMP plenary runs from 22 to 25 June at EMA headquarters in Amsterdam. PRAC meets on 8 to 11 June and COMP on 16 to 18 June. If your company has a file in the queue, this is the window to confirm your rapporteur engagement plan. Brubru's My EU Calendar carries every 2026 date for CHMP, PRAC, COMP, CAT, PDCO and HMPC, filterable by committee.
headlines.ask: When does the EMA CHMP next meet, and what are all the 2026 plenary dates?

headlines.title: The Commission extended Hungary's and Poland's emergency medicine measures
headlines.source: Official Journal, Commission Implementing Decisions 2026/1182 and 2026/1104, late May 2026
headlines.snippet: Two implementing decisions extending Member State emergency action on specific medicinal products were published this week, one for Hungary and one for Poland. The legal basis is Article 5(1) of Directive 2001/83/EC, the route that lets a national authority keep a product available outside the standard authorisation track. Companies with portfolios touching either market should map the affected products. Brubru can pull the consolidated text on request.
headlines.ask: What did the Commission extend with Implementing Decisions 2026/1182 and 2026/1104, and what is Article 5(1) of Directive 2001/83/EC?

headlines.title: The Health Security Committee met on 24 May, summary report now public
headlines.source: DG SANTE Health Security Committee summary report, Tuesday 26 May 2026
headlines.snippet: The senior-level Health Security Committee, the body that coordinates Member State and Commission action on serious cross-border health threats, met on 24 May. The summary report covers preparedness, surveillance, and joint procurement. EFPIA's vaccines and antimicrobial members watch this layer for early signals on the next joint-procurement waves. DG SANTE also flagged a Prevention Subgroup meeting on lifelong prevention held on 22 May.
headlines.ask: What did the EU Health Security Committee discuss on 24 May 2026, and how does joint procurement work under Decision 1082/2013/EU?

headlines.title: Brubru is tracking the Critical Medicines Act, now a provisional deal
headlines.snippet: The Critical Medicines Act procedure 2025/0102(COD) reached a provisional inter-institutional agreement on 11 and 12 May under the Cyprus Council Presidency. It is not yet adopted, the legal-linguistic clean-up and the formal adoption votes still have to happen. The main change worth carrying: the threshold of Member States needed to ask the Commission to procure on their behalf dropped from nine to five. Tomislav Sokol (EPP, Croatia) stays the SANT rapporteur, with the same shadow team that worked the December report.
headlines.ask: What is the current status of the Critical Medicines Act trilogue, and what changed in the joint-procurement threshold?
